paragraphs.text: A purpose-trained intfloat/e5-base-v2 retriever, using chunking and the maximum score over chunks, ranked installed effects much more faithfully than the length baseline across six sources and both polarities; averaging over chunks produced the same strong correlation at both polarities. This pattern was not explained by document length because retriever scores were negatively correlated with word count. Nevertheless, these are rank correlations rather than attributable fractions, and no removal experiment was run for this retriever. The comparison therefore bounds the verdict to gradient-based attribution: content-keyed methods need not treat content-matched but effect-divergent sources alike, yet ranking fidelity alone cannot establish removal efficacy, as the seed contradiction for delta-predictability illustrates.
